english: You watch voluntarily.
tip: olarak means as or in the role of and turns a word into an adverb: gönüllü olarak means voluntarily, as a volunteer.

english: The teacher is looking at the new bicycle.
tip: bakmak (to look) needs -e/-a on its object: bisiklete bakıyor means looking at the bicycle, never a plain object form.

english: I want you to be happy.
tip: To say I want you to do something, use verb+ma plus a possessive and -ı: olmanı istiyorum means I want you to be.

english: The firefighter usually gets up early.
tip: The aorist -r marks habits and routines, not this moment: kalkar means gets up as a rule, matching genellikle (usually).

english: I enjoy walking in the forest in autumn.
tip: sevmek takes its object in -i, so walking becomes yürümeyi (yürü+me+yi): yürümeyi seviyorum means I like walking.

english: I'll stop by the market after leaving work.
tip: Add -ınca to a verb for when or as soon as: çıkınca means once I leave. İşten çıkınca means after leaving work.

english: The bus didn't come, let's take a taxi.
tip: The ending -elim/-alım means let's: bin (get on) becomes binelim, meaning let's get on.

english: I'll go for a walk when the rain stops.
tip: Verb + -dığında means when that happens: durduğunda means when it stops. Yağmur durduğunda, when the rain stops.

english: I'm going to meet with my friends this weekend.
tip: The -ş in buluşmak makes it reciprocal, done to each other: buluşacağım means I'll meet up with someone, not meet alone.

english: He is waiting seriously.
tip: adjective + bir şekilde builds a manner phrase like English -ly: ciddi bir şekilde means seriously, in a serious way.

english: You went to school just now.
tip: az önce means a moment ago and pairs with the simple past: gittin means you went, so the sentence says you just went.

english: I walk to school every day.
tip: Verb + -erek says by doing, describing how: yürüyerek means by walking, on foot. yürüyerek giderim, I go on foot.

english: Giving wrong information can be dangerous.
tip: -abil means can or might: olabilir means it can be or may be. tehlikeli olabilir, it could be dangerous.

english: The children returned home from school happily.
tip: Pair -den (from) with -e (to) for a route: okuldan eve means from school to home.

english: We will stay at the hotel next year.
tip: önümüzdeki literally means the one in front of us and is how Turkish says next: önümüzdeki yıl means next year.

english: He apparently got sick, didn't come to work.
tip: The -mış past reports something inferred or heard, not witnessed: olmuş and gelmemiş mean he apparently got sick, didn't come.

target: Ben iki gün önce havaalanında check-in yaptım.
english: I checked in at the airport two days ago.
tip: After a length of time, önce means ago: iki gün önce means two days ago.

target: Komşumuzun kedisi bizim bahçeye sürekli geliyor.
english: Our neighbor's cat keeps coming to our garden.
tip: Possession links two nouns: the owner takes -ın, the thing takes -si. Komşumuzun kedisi means our neighbor's cat.

target: Dağın arkasında küçük bir köy var.
english: There is a small village behind the mountain.
tip: To say behind, the thing takes -ın and arka takes -sında: Dağın arkasında means behind the mountain.

target: Doğru cevabı bulmak için dikkatli düşünmeliyiz.
english: We must think carefully to find the correct answer.
tip: Infinitive + için means in order to: cevabı bulmak için means in order to find the answer.

target: İstiyorum ki antrenman daha sıkı olsun.
english: I want the training to be tougher.
tip: ki opens a wished-for clause whose verb ends in -sın: İstiyorum ki ... olsun means I want it to be, with olsun as let it be.

target: Sabah işe giderken trafik çok yoğundu.
english: Traffic was very heavy going to work in the morning.
tip: Verb + -ken means while doing: giderken means while going. işe giderken, while going to work.

target: Yengemle çok iyi anlaşıyoruz, arkadaş gibiyiz.
english: I get along very well with my sister-in-law, we're like friends.
tip: gibi means like or similar to and follows the noun it compares: arkadaş gibiyiz means we are like friends.

target: Dün gece çok güzel bir rüya gördüm.
english: I had a very nice dream last night.
tip: Turkish sees a dream rather than has one: rüya gördüm is literally I saw a dream, the normal way to say I dreamed.

target: Güzel bir gün geçirmek için planlarım var.
english: I have plans to spend a nice day.
tip: var means there is or, with a possessive, have: planlarım var means I have plans, literally my plans exist.

target: Her sabah işe gitmeden önce spor yapıyorum.
english: I exercise every morning before going to work.
tip: Verb + -meden önce means before doing: gitmeden önce means before going. işe gitmeden önce, before going to work.

target: Bu mevsimde mandalina çok ucuz ve tatlı.
english: Mandarins are very cheap and sweet this season.
tip: Turkish drops the verb to be in the present: mandalina çok ucuz is literally mandarin very cheap, meaning mandarins are cheap.

target: Ev ile okul arasında bir park var.
english: There is a park between the house and school.
tip: arasında means between and follows both nouns joined by ile: Ev ile okul arasında means between the house and the school.

target: Ailemiz küçük ama çok mutlu bir ailedir.
english: Our family is small but a very happy family.
tip: The ending -dir adds a formal, matter-of-fact tone: ailedir means it is a family, stated as a general truth.

target: Damlaya damlaya göl olur, az az biriktir.
english: Drop by drop a lake forms; save little by little.
tip: Repeating a word builds a step-by-step sense: damlaya damlaya means drop by drop, showing a gradual action.
